theme: A quiet Sunday on the water.
greeting: You're mid-charter on the Adriatic, Dan — an open Sunday with only a 15-minute check-in with Mike on the books. The Florida-trip logistics can wait until you're back on dry land.

needsAttention.title: Florida car still unbooked
needsAttention.detail: The Sept 20–Oct 5 full-size SUV out of Tampa is now a firm need rather than a hedge — flagged p1 and past due. One to lock whenever you next get a solid signal ashore.

needsAttention.title: St Pete landing nights open
needsAttention.detail: You land Tampa Sept 20 but the kids aren't picked up until the 22nd, so the nights of Sept 20–21 near St Pete still need a room. p1, past due.

needsAttention.title: Cavtat transfer and early checkout
needsAttention.detail: Disembark is noon Sept 19 at Komolac with a 5:15 AM airport run the next morning — the Cavtat transfer and express checkout are still open and best sorted from shore before connectivity thins out.

schedule.title: Sunday review with Mike
schedule.detail: 15-min pass over the board — owners, dates, promote or kill. Meet link is on the invite.

flagged.title: VP Government Affairs roles surfaced
flagged.detail: LinkedIn flagged a NYT VP, Government Affairs opening and an EU AI Act SVP, Strategy posting — both squarely in your lane.

flagged.title: ICGN Toronto conference booking open
flagged.detail: Registration is underway for the ICGN Autumn Conference in Toronto this November — a governance-network fit worth a look.

inbox.noise: The rest is newsletters and retail — Breeze fares, Choosing Keeping, Slightly Foxed, a Patreon post, and the Valoris dispatch.
inbox.clear: Nothing in the inbox is waiting on your reply.

recipe.title: Chicken and Chickpea Tagine
recipe.why: A warming, spice-laced braise for the first properly cool Maine evening of the season — slow, fragrant, and forgiving of a quiet Sunday at the stove.

tasks.title: Confirm Nautilus return transfer to the airport
Sort Orlando Disney tickets for the six of you

acts.line: A short board review with Mike at 9, and nothing else claims the hours after it.
Open water and open time — the charter is the only thing on the agenda.
No commitments on the books; the day closes whenever you want it to.
